chapter: Keppard, Oliver and the Magnolia band
title: The Magnolia band at Huntson Nagel's Casino
summary: Personnel of Oliver's Magnolia band at the Casino dance hall, Louis Keppard's brief stay, and the Hunts and Nagel ownership.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: And you remember who else was in the band with Oliver when you worked with him and where

you played? Uh, let's see now. We played so many different, we was playing spot job. We didn't have no sound plays until we went to Hunson Nagel. Now, uh, let's see. What color was this, Hunson Nagel? He had, uh, Liberty in the Outerville. Liberty. He's band, he had, uh, uh, Call it the Casino. Oh yeah. He had, uh, Chris Kelly. Uh, no, uh, he had, uh, uh, Chris Miner on the drum. And he had, uh, uh, Alphonse Piku. And, uh, Joe Atkins. Uh, Joe Atkins. Uh. Joe Atkins. Uh. Joe Atkins. Ed Atkins. Ed Atkins was, yeah. On trombone that one. Yeah, on trombone. I was playing guitar. He had, uh, he had, uh, Pop Foster on the bass. Uh, he had Pop Foster's brother Willie Foster on the violin. That's it.
That was the Magnolia band. Do you remember, uh, I think, uh, Louie Kepard tells me that he played in the Magnolia band too with Oliver for a while.
He played, he played, he played, he played, he played, he played a little while, yeah. But he didn't play long. He ain't, he wasn't much of him. He played a little while.
Uh huh. And you played guitar then, but that was before Louie Kepard then, you joined him.
Uh, did you play any later jobs, any place much in the district with Joe or other places?
No, the only place where I played them was right down in Ponsonagle then. Uh huh.
At the casino. Was that sort of a cabaret, what was it, uh, or? The dance hall. It was the dance hall. It was the local dance hall. And dance hall and dance hall. Hmm.

And it was the casino dance hall, but it ran by Hunts. Hunts, uh, and Eddie Groeschel. Yeah, that's right. And they called it Hunts and Nagels. Yeah, that's right. Hunts and Nagels. Hunts and Nagels, they called it like that. Yeah. Through Hunts. Yeah, that's right. And Eddie Groeschel. Eddie Groeschel was his partner. It was his partnership. He was a partnership. But the name of it was the casino. Yeah, that's the casino.
